questions.question: How do Shapley values attribute feature importance?
questions.answer: Shapley values attribute feature importance by averaging a feature's marginal contributions across all possible orderings of the features [1]. This is done by generating many predictions based on a partial set of the features used by the model and comparing the results of the predicted values [2]. The Shapley value is then calculated by averaging the contributions from each step on the path to arrive at a value that represents the feature's influence on the prediction [3].

questions.question: Who published the Shapley value technique and when?
questions.answer: Lloyd Shapley published the Shapley value technique in 1951 [1]. He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics in 2012 for his contributions to cooperative game theory, which includes the Shapley value technique [1].

questions.question: What are the main hyperparameter tuning strategies?
questions.answer: The three main hyperparameter tuning strategies are grid search, random search, and Bayesian search. Grid search involves selecting a range of candidate values for the hyperparameters and then training a model for each set of hyperparameters [1]. Random search involves randomly selecting a subset of the candidate models and then training a model for each of those selected models [5]. Bayesian search, also known as Bayesian optimization, involves randomly training a small number of candidate models and then using the evaluation metrics of those models to choose the next set of candidate models [4].

questions.question: How do you get a score function for hyperparameter tuning in scikit-learn?
questions.answer: You can get a score function for hyperparameter tuning in scikit-learn by taking the negative RMSE instead [1]. This allows you to use the score function for hyperparameter tuning, which is set to use score functions by default in scikit-learn [2].

questions.answer: To create a hyperparameter tuning job with the CREATE MODEL statement, you need to specify the optimizer being used with the optimizer='adagrad' option [1]. The statement for creating a hyperparameter tuning job is very similar to what you used before, with some key differences for the sake of hyperparameter tuning [2]. questions.question: Why should you consider deployment when choosing which model to train?
questions.answer: When choosing which model to train, you should consider deployment because the end goal of your model is to provide a valuable service to people who will use it, and deployment is crucial to ensure that your model can be used effectively [1]. This includes considering factors such as prediction latency, deployment options, and the ability to interact with the model, as well as the trade-offs between different deployment approaches [2].

questions.question: How do you validate that a deployed model keeps learning something useful?
questions.answer: You can validate that a deployed model keeps learning something useful by tracking when its performance drifts, ideally by bringing it back to business metrics such as usage metrics [1]. Another approach is to track the uncertainty of the model or monitor its performance over time to detect any changes [2]. Additionally, you can use explainability techniques to monitor deployed models for drift and skew in their predictions, indicating when a model should be retrained [6].

questions.question: What is client-side deployment?
questions.answer: Client-side deployment is a method of deploying machine learning models where all computations are run on the client device, eliminating the need for a server to run models. This approach reduces the need to build infrastructure that can run inference for every single user, reduces network latency, and can even allow an application to run with no access to the network [1, 6]. It also removes the need to transfer sensitive data to a remote server [6].

questions.question: What is the goal of deploying a model?
questions.answer: The goal of deploying a model is to allow users to interact with it, providing a valuable service to people who will use it [1]. This involves considering factors such as prediction latency, model performance, and potential misuse of the model [2]. Deploying a model also requires careful consideration of failure modes and safeguards to mitigate errors [3].
